feature_results.rationale: GitHub Copilot exposes an admin-accessible audit log for organization and enterprise administrators, covering Copilot-related configuration changes (plan/policy/settings changes, seat assignment/removal) and activity. Events are searchable with the `action:copilot` qualifier, and a documented reference lists the full set of Copilot audit log event types, including a separate reference for agent-related audit events. This is admin/org-level oversight (not a personal client-side history), so it meets the has_criteria. Coverage is tied to the organization/enterprise audit log surface used by Copilot Business/Enterprise plans.

evidence.excerpt: You can use the audit log to review actions taken in your enterprise, including changes to your Copilot plan, such as changes to settings and policies or a user losing or receiving a license. ... action:copilot returns all GitHub Copilot audit log events for your organization or enterprise. ... The audit log does not include client session data, such as the prompts a user sends to Copilot locally.
Audit log events for agents

constraints.description: Audit log review for Copilot is documented for organization/enterprise admins on Copilot Business (and Enterprise); it is an org/enterprise audit-log surface, not a feature of an individual Free/Pro personal account.
The audit log excludes client-session data (e.g., prompts sent to Copilot locally); Enterprise Cloud docs cite retention of Copilot Business plan events for a 180-day window.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub officially documents a dedicated Copilot code review workflow, distinct from ad-hoc chat: a reviewer can request a Copilot review on a pull request (or configure automatic re-review on every push via repository rules), and Copilot returns review comments with suggested changes that can be applied directly, including a 'Fix with Copilot' follow-up action. The capability reached general availability in April 2025 and has continued to receive dedicated updates (e.g. AGENTS.md support, customization via REVIEW.md/CLAUDE.md, CLI-initiated reviews) through mid-2026. It is scoped to paid Copilot plans.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot typically finishes reviewing in less than 30 seconds.
GitHub Copilot can review pull requests in your enterprise to save time for human reviewers by detecting bugs or vulnerabilities and enforcing consistent coding standards.
Copilot code review now generally available

constraints.description: Copilot code review is documented as available with the Copilot Pro, Copilot Pro+, Copilot Business, and Copilot Enterprise plans, not the free tier, with the exception of single-selection-in-file review in VS Code which is available to all Copilot users.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Copilot documents multiple autonomous, multi-step execution surfaces: IDE 'agent mode' independently decides which files to change, applies edits and terminal commands, and iterates until the task is complete without per-step confirmation; the Copilot CLI's 'autopilot' mode carries out multiple steps toward a task without waiting for user input after each step; and Copilot cloud/coding agent works autonomously end-to-end on issues. This matches the has_criteria (decomposes a task into steps, executes autonomously, reports back on completion) and goes beyond a single accepted suggestion.

evidence.excerpt: In agent mode, Copilot determines which files to make changes to, offers code changes and terminal commands to complete the task, and iterates to remediate issues until the original task is complete.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Copilot's cloud/coding agent is documented as an asynchronous, background task system: a task is delegated (from an issue, PR comment, or chat), the agent works in its own GitHub Actions-powered environment for minutes to hours without occupying the user's active session, and it opens/updates a pull request and requests review on completion. This is a general-purpose background execution mechanism (not limited to a narrow task type like tests only), matching the has_criteria and going beyond a synchronous, UI-blocking operation.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub documents two complementary whole-repository, meaning-based retrieval mechanisms rather than plain text search: (1) Copilot Chat automatically indexes the current repository so that questions are answered using context-enriched understanding of the code's structure and logic (GitHub.com and VS Code), and (2) the Copilot coding (cloud) agent uses semantic code search to find relevant code by meaning rather than exact text matches such as grep, applied automatically with no configuration when it does not know precise names or patterns. Copilot Spaces likewise retrieve only the most relevant repository content for a query instead of loading the whole project.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot cloud agent uses semantic code search to find relevant code based on meaning, rather than relying solely on exact text matches with tools like grep.

When you start a conversation with Copilot Chat that has a repository context, the repository is automatically indexed to improve context-enriched answers to your questions about the code's structure and logic in GitHub and Visual Studio Code.

constraints.description: Automatic repository indexing for Copilot Chat is documented for GitHub.com and Visual Studio Code specifically; semantic code search is documented as a mechanism of the Copilot coding (cloud) agent rather than a uniformly-named feature across every Copilot surface.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub documents concrete, actionable data-use controls that differ by plan tier: individual-plan subscribers (Free, Pro, Pro+, Max) have a personal settings toggle to opt out of having their Copilot interaction data used for model training; GitHub states it does not use Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise customer data to train models at all, with that exclusion backed by GitHub's Data Protection Agreement. This is a concrete, documented control (not generic privacy-policy language), meeting the has_criteria, though the mechanism differs across tiers (opt-out toggle vs. contractual non-use).

evidence.excerpt: GitHub may use your interactions with GitHub features and services—including inputs, outputs, code snippets, and associated context—to train and improve AI models. ... You can opt-out from allowing your data to be used for training in your personal settings for GitHub Copilot. ... GitHub does not use Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise customer data to train AI models.
Managing GitHub Copilot policies as an individual subscriber

constraints.description: The mechanism differs by plan: Copilot Free/Pro/Pro+/Max individual subscribers must set a personal opt-out preference to exclude their data from training; Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise customer data is excluded from training by default under GitHub's Data Protection Agreement rather than via a toggle.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Copilot's Edits/Edit mode workflow shows AI-generated changes across one or more files as inline diffs that must be explicitly accepted before they are written to disk, with per-file and per-turn accept/reject controls documented on GitHub's own docs and corroborated by the changelog announcement and Microsoft's first-party Visual Studio documentation for the same feature (Tab-to-accept / Alt+Delete-to-reject at the individual-change level). This satisfies has_criteria and goes beyond the partial_criteria's whole-file-only limitation.

evidence.excerpt: Edit mode is recommended when you want more granular control over the edits that Copilot proposes, where you choose which files Copilot can make changes to, provide context to Copilot with each iteration, and decide whether or not to accept the suggested edits after each turn.
These edits are applied directly in the editor, so you can quickly review them in place, with the full context of the surrounding code.
You can use the Tab key to accept a proposal, Alt+Delete to reject a proposal, or F8 to go to the next proposal.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Copilot documents both elements the taxonomy asks for. (1) A configurable duplication-detection filter blocks Copilot code suggestions that match or near-match public code on GitHub (checked at roughly 65 lexemes / 150 characters); it can be set as a personal preference or enforced as an organization/enterprise-wide policy. (2) GitHub/Microsoft extend the 'Copilot Copyright Commitment' IP indemnification to paid Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise customers: GitHub's own Product Specific Terms for these plans incorporate the Microsoft Customer Copyright Commitment, under which GitHub/Microsoft will defend the customer and cover adverse judgments or settlements for third-party IP claims arising from unmodified Copilot output, conditioned on the built-in duplication filter/guardrails being enabled. The indemnity commitment is documented as applying to the paid commercial (Business/Enterprise) terms specifically, not to other/free usage governed by the general Terms of Service.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot checks code suggestions for matches or near-matches against public code on GitHub of 65 lexemes or more (on average, 150 characters). If there is a match, the suggestion will not be shown to the user.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub documents both a retrieval-based mechanism for large repositories and an extended-context model option, going beyond a bare model context-window figure. feature_results.rationale: GitHub's own documentation describes a supported sub-agent orchestration mechanism: custom agents are attached to a session (own system prompt, tool restrictions, optional MCP servers), and when a request matches a custom agent's expertise the Copilot runtime automatically delegates to it as a sub-agent running in an isolated context, with lifecycle events streamed back to the parent session. This is documented as a supported mechanism (Copilot SDK / Copilot CLI custom agents), not an undocumented or experimental flag, matching the has_criteria for delegation to multiple coordinated sub-agents.

evidence.excerpt: When a user's request matches an agent's expertise, the Copilot runtime automatically delegates to that agent as a sub-agent—running it in an isolated context while streaming lifecycle events back to the parent session.

Work performed by a custom agent is carried out using a subagent, which is a temporary agent spun up to complete the task. The subagent has its own context window, which can be populated by information that is not relevant to the main agent.

constraints.description: Documented sub-agent orchestration (custom agents delegated as isolated-context sub-agents) is described for the Copilot SDK and Copilot CLI surface; this bundle did not find equivalent documentation confirming the same orchestration mechanism for the plain IDE chat/agent-mode surface.

feature_results.rationale: GitHub Copilot's core AI service is delivered as multi-tenant SaaS: GitHub's own documentation on model hosting and on Copilot data residency describes Copilot inference as routed to GitHub/Microsoft-operated or partner (AWS, Anthropic, Google Cloud, OpenAI, Azure) cloud endpoints, with region-level data-residency controls but no option to run Copilot inference on customer-owned infrastructure. Separately, Microsoft/GitHub have introduced 'GitHub Enterprise Local' (currently in public preview), a distinctly branded enterprise product built on Azure Local that can run fully on customer-owned infrastructure, including in disconnected/air-gapped deployments. In connected mode it uses the same cloud-hosted Copilot; in disconnected mode AI assistance is instead delivered via local inference endpoints, described by the vendor as providing 'a similar experience' rather than confirmed feature parity with hosted Copilot. Because private/on-prem deployment is available only via this separately branded, preview-stage product line, with parity of the AI experience explicitly qualified rather than guaranteed, this matches the partial criteria rather than a full has.

evidence.excerpt: GitHub routes all Copilot requests to model endpoints within your enterprise's designated region, and your code, prompts, and Copilot responses never leave your region during inference processing.

GitHub Enterprise Local is fully hosted on customer owned infrastructure ... In disconnected deployments, GitHub Enterprise Local runs entirely within your infrastructure, with all functionalities operating locally and without external service dependencies ... Connected environments leverage cloud-hosted AI (for example, GitHub Copilot and GitHub CLI) ... disconnected (air-gapped) environments maintain a similar experience by using GitHub CLI-style workflows paired with local inference endpoints (for example, Foundry Local).
